title: Ar-Rahim, the Most Compassionate
hookLine: the Most Compassionate, mercy that reaches each one, closely

lines: WOULD SHE THROW IT IN A FIRE?
cards: After a battle, captives are brought into Medina. Among them is a woman who is frantic, searching every face. She has lost her baby.
Whenever she finds a small child among the captives, she lifts it, presses it to her chest and feeds it.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is watching with his companions, and Bukhari and Muslim record what he asked them: do you think this woman would ever throw her child into a fire? They said, no, never, not if she could help it.
Yesterday was mercy like the rain, falling on everything. Today is mercy like that mother's arms.

teach.b: The Prophet said: Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child.
Ar-Rahim comes from the same root as ar-Rahman, r-h-m, and the two almost always travel together: bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim, in every surah but one.
So why two names from one root? Scholars have given several answers, and they fit together. The form of ar-Rahman means full and overflowing.
The form of ar-Rahim, fa'il, means ongoing, the one who keeps on doing it.

teach.h: VAST AS THE SKY; ARRIVING TODAY.
teach.b: So ar-Rahman is mercy as vast as the sky; ar-Rahim is mercy that arrives, that reaches this particular person, today.
Many commentators add a second difference: ar-Rahman is mercy for all creation in this world, and ar-Rahim a special mercy for the believers, especially in the next.
The Qur'an says in al-Ahzab that He is ever merciful to the believers, rahim. Here's a surprise. Unlike ar-Rahman, the word rahim can describe a person.
In Surah at-Tawbah the Prophet himself is called ra'uf rahim, kind and merciful to the believers.
That makes Ar-Rahim a name you can imitate, and the Prophet said so, in Tirmidhi's collection: the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful.
Have mercy on those on the earth, and the One above will have mercy on you. Mercy close up isn't an idea. It's a mother holding a child close.

how: Muslims say ar-Rahim with ar-Rahman in every bismillah, and many take the hadith of the merciful being shown mercy as a daily rule: kindness to family, neighbors, strangers and animals.

o: mercy that keeps arriving, close to each one
the same mercy as ar-Rahman, said twice
mercy shown only after a person repents

games.q: the two names — tap the pairs.
p: more merciful is Allah than she

s: ar-Rahim, like ar-Rahman, can never describe a person
at-Tawbah calls the Prophet ra'uf rahim, kind and merciful.
the bismillah opens every surah but one
ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim come from different roots
both from r-h-m; they differ in form.

games.q: the Prophet points to a mother holding her child and asks: would she throw it in a fire? what does he say next?
o: Allah is more merciful to His servants than she is to her child
games.why: Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman to her child (Bukhari; Muslim).

practice: Bring to mind one person who could use a little mercy today, someone struggling, tired, alone, or carrying something nobody sees, and picture their face.
Then picture one small, specific thing you could do for them, a message, a coffee, not correcting them this once, letting them go first; keep it tiny and real, and hold the picture for a few breaths.
If you pray, you can ask ar-Rahim for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Ar-Rahim. The Most Compassionate: mercy that keeps on arriving, reaching each one closely, and a mercy people are asked to imitate. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Most Compassionate, mercy that keeps on reaching; from r-h-m.

carryVoice: Your line: mercy close up. It's the kind of mercy you can pass on. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5999; Sahih Muslim 2754 (the captive mother and her child)
Qur'an 33:43 (He is ever merciful to the believers)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1924 (the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful)
